title: pi-auto-rename: direct endpoint support + Oqto RPC fixes
description:
On oqto-azure multi-user deployment, all sessions show 'New Session' because:

1. The endpoint field in auto-rename.json is completely ignored by the extension code. It only knows the Pi model registry.
2. debugNotify() uses ctx.ui.notify() which is invisible in Oqto RPC mode, so all failures are silent.
3. checkExistingName() only skips 'chat' but may treat other default-like names as already-renamed.

Fix:
- Add endpoint field support: direct HTTP fetch to OpenAI-compatible endpoint (e.g. local llama.cpp on :8090) without requiring the model in models.json.
- Make debugNotify() also log to console when !ctx.hasUI (or always when debug=true).
- Treat common defaults ('New Session', 'chat', 'untitled') as not-yet-renamed.
- Update schema.json.

3. Frontend should show a generated title, not 'New Session'.
4. Check llama-server logs on :8090 to confirm title requests arrive.

pi-inline-macros: Composable Prompt Macros with ::name Syntax
description:
Enable composable prompt instructions via an inline `::macroName` syntax that expands prompt templates anywhere in a user message. Works identically in TUI and RPC modes by leveraging the `input` event and extension command APIs.

The extension should reuse the existing prompt template pool (global, project, package, settings, CLI) so users do not need to maintain a separate macro registry. When a user types `::review`, the extension replaces it with the content of `review.md` before the message reaches the LLM.

This must work in both interactive TUI mode and programmatic RPC/SDK mode, with feature parity for expansion, listing, and insertion.
close_reason: Implemented pi-inline-macros extension with ::name inline expansion via input transform, reusing loaded prompt template commands (global/project/package/settings/CLI), plus docs update.

title: Core expansion engine
description:
Implement the `input` event handler that expands `::macroName` tokens before skill/template expansion.

Requirements:
- Regex: `(?:^|\s)::([a-zA-Z][-\w]*)\b` so `std::io` and CSS `::before` are ignored
- Expand all occurrences in the message body, not just the first
- Load template content from the same discovery paths as built-in prompt templates
- Support `$1`, `$2`, `$@` positional arguments: `::review HEAD~3` passes `HEAD~3` as `$1`
- If a macro is not found, leave the token as-is and append a warning note, or replace with an error marker
- Detect and prevent infinite recursion (macro A expands to macro B which references A)
- Return `{ action: "transform", text }` from the input handler
- Must work when session is invoked via `session.prompt()` in RPC/SDK mode, not just TUI typing
close_reason: Implemented input transform expansion engine for ::name with required regex semantics, multi-occurrence expansion, positional args (//), unknown-token preservation, recursion cycle detection, and RPC/TUI compatibility via input event.

2. Widget below editor: on every input event, scan for ::name tokens. Show a confirmation strip listing resolved macros (name + description) in accent bold. Strip omitted when no macros detected. Placement: belowEditor so it doesn't compete with messages.

Why lean: no editor component replacement, no cursor math, composes safely with any other extension. All styling done via setWidget and addAutocompleteProvider APIs.

title: privileged command extension: preserve caller PATH and improve TTY/auth diagnostics
description:
Observed behavior
- Running privileged workflows via the extension can fail with misleading downstream errors because PATH differs from the normal shell.
- Example from oqto_refactor deploy flow: privileged execution failed with `remote-build: command not found` until PATH was manually injected.
- Related friction: when command requires interactive auth/TTY semantics, failure messages are not explicit enough for quick remediation.

Expected behavior
1) Preserve or explicitly reconstruct caller PATH (including user-local bins like ~/.local/bin) by default.
2) On failures related to interactivity/TTY, return explicit diagnostic guidance instead of opaque command-not-found cascades.
3) Provide opt-in strict mode if security policy wants minimal PATH.

Why this matters
- Agents rely on the privileged extension for root-required commands; PATH drift creates non-deterministic failures and wasted debugging cycles.
- Better diagnostics materially improve recovery speed in CI-like and agentic workflows.

Suggested acceptance criteria
- Repro command using user-local binary succeeds under privileged extension without manual PATH export.
- Error payload differentiates PATH resolution failure vs auth/TTY failure.
- Docs include PATH/security tradeoffs and recommended defaults.

- Root cause is ambiguity between transient retry errors vs terminal durable errors across streamed events.

Goal

- Provide fixtures/examples to validate the contract in integrations.

Proposed scope
1) Document expected semantics:
   - recoverable retry errors: frontend turn-local persistence only (not durable history rows)
   - terminal errors: exactly one durable assistant error message (typed error part)
   - no empty assistant placeholder artifacts
2) Provide machine-readable event sequence fixtures for:
   - retry->success
   - retry exhausted terminal failure
   - immediate terminal failure
3) Add extension-side validation helper or sample tests that consumers can copy.

Why in pi-agent-extensions
- This repo is a practical integration surface used by agent runtimes and extension authors.
- Having canonical fixtures/docs here can reduce protocol drift and prevent repeated downstream regressions.

pi-auto-rename: avoid stale extension ctx crash after fast prompt sessions
description:
Observed behavior
- Running a short one-shot prompt can complete successfully and then crash in the `pi-auto-rename` extension.
- Repro command from installed extension environment:

```bash
cd ~/.pi/agent
pi -p "hello" --model zgx/qwen3.6-35b
```

- The model response is printed, then Node exits with:

```text
Error: This extension ctx is stale after session replacement or reload. Do not use a captured pi or command ctx after ctx.newSession(), ctx.fork(), ctx.switchSession(), or ctx.reload(). For newSession, fork, and switchSession, move post-replacement work into withSession and use the ctx passed to withSession. For reload, do not use the old ctx after await ctx.reload().
    at Object.assertActive (.../dist/core/extensions/loader.js:131:19)
    at Object.setSessionName (.../dist/core/extensions/loader.js:235:21)
    at setNameAndNotify (~/.pi/agent/extensions/pi-auto-rename/index.ts:1001:8)
    at renameFromQuery (~/.pi/agent/extensions/pi-auto-rename/index.ts:1060:5)
```

Likely root cause
- `pi-auto-rename/index.ts` starts async rename work from `before_agent_start` without awaiting it:

```ts
void renameFromQuery(prompt, ctx);
```

- For fast non-interactive sessions (`pi -p "hello"`), the session may finish/reload/replace before `generateSessionName(...)` returns.
- The async continuation later calls `setNameAndNotify(fullName, ctx)`, which calls `pi.setSessionName(name)` after the extension context has become stale.

Expected behavior
- Auto-rename must never crash the pi process after a successful short prompt.
- If the session context becomes inactive before rename finishes, the extension should skip the rename gracefully or use the current supported with-session/session-replacement API pattern.
- One-shot CLI prompts should exit 0 when the agent turn itself succeeds.

Suggested fix directions
1. Do not fire-and-forget context-dependent rename work from `before_agent_start`; await it if acceptable for UX, or move post-replacement work into the supported `withSession` pattern if available.
2. Add a guard around late rename completion so stale-context errors are swallowed/logged as debug warnings rather than crashing the process.
3. Audit other `pi.setSessionName(...)` call sites in `pi-auto-rename/index.ts` for the same stale-context risk.
4. Prefer using the `ctx` passed to the active hook/session callback for all UI/status operations; do not retain it across session replacement/reload boundaries.

Acceptance criteria
- Add a regression test or scripted repro that runs a fast one-shot command with auto-rename enabled, e.g. `pi -p "hello" --model <available-fast-model>`, and verifies no stale ctx exception is thrown.
- Verify both `prefixOnly` and generated-name modes do not crash when the session ends quickly.
- Verify interactive sessions still get renamed as before.
- Verify non-TUI/Oqto status notification behavior still emits title-change status only when the context is active.
- Run repo validation: `bun run check`.

Notes
- Installed failing code path observed around `~/.pi/agent/extensions/pi-auto-rename/index.ts:1001` and `:1060`.
- Similar direct calls also appear earlier in the extension around the prefix/generated-name rename paths; include them in the audit.
close_reason: Fixed by guarding all pi.setSessionName and ctx.ui.setStatus calls against stale extension context errors. Added isStaleContextError helper, wrapped setNameAndNotify and handleRegen post-await paths with try/catch, and added regression tests. Version bumped to 1.2.1.

Oqto is moving to a canonical, lossless timeline architecture where `oqto-log` is authoritative and hstry is a derived projection/search layer. The bridge extension should provide high-quality native signals, but must not become the durable authority.

## Goal

Make `pi-oqto-bridge` a better observer for Oqto's timeline assembler by emitting structured lifecycle/status events that are deterministic, correlated, and replay-friendly.

## Required event families

Emit observer-only status events, preferably through the existing `ctx.ui.setStatus(QUEUE_EVENT_KEY, JSON.stringify(...))` path unless a better Pi extension mechanism exists.

Lifecycle events to add where Pi hooks expose enough data:

Every emitted event should include as many of these as are safely available:

title: Implement Pi A2UI extension with complete v0.9.1 protocol and broker semantics
description:
## Outcome

Implement an operator-owned `pi-a2ui` extension that adapts Pi's native extension API to Oqto's host-neutral A2UI Presentation Broker and supports the complete production A2UI v0.9.1 protocol surface. The extension is the Pi-specific adapter only: it does not render UI, own durable presentation state, or bypass Oqto authorization.

Official baseline: `a2ui-project/a2ui` production v0.9.1 at commit `fd12863d7ecd8aeb3b0dc8960757e2fe90a63ca9`. Track v1.0 separately after it leaves release-candidate status; structure the adapter so protocol codecs are versioned rather than hard-coded into Pi behavior.

Research reference: `utensils/aethon` commit `12ffdc13` proves Pi-native inspect/mutate tools and structured UI event routing, but its same-process/no-permission trust model and prose `session.prompt()` response path must not be copied.

## Required architecture

- Create a self-contained extension directory (for example `pi-a2ui/`) following this repository's extension conventions, with README, configuration schema/example, tests, and changelog/version updates.
- Register focused Pi tools through `pi.registerTool()` for presentation lifecycle and inspection. Tool schemas must be strict TypeBox schemas—no `any`/`Type.Any`, unknown fields, arbitrary callbacks, DOM selectors, or raw host-store access.
- Communicate only with the Runner Capability Broker over an inherited/session-bound operator-owned channel. Do not read work-directory control sockets, credentials, Oqto frontend stores, or browser state.
- Preserve canonical Oqto identifiers and attribution: Session, Presentation, Surface, Component, Action, Interaction, revision, acting Account/requester, and originating tool call. Pi session IDs remain adapter-local.
- Support cancellation through the tool `AbortSignal`, broker disconnect, Pi session shutdown/switch/fork, and presentation deletion. Pending waits must have explicit timeout/cancel semantics and leave no orphan listeners.
- Dynamically activate tools only when the broker advertises the capability; fail closed with actionable errors when unavailable or when protocol/catalog versions are unsupported.

## Full A2UI v0.9.1 coverage

### Server-to-client presentation stream

Support and strictly validate every envelope and lifecycle operation:

- `createSurface`: surface ID, catalog ID, root component ID, initial components, initial data model, theme and styles according to the negotiated catalog.
- `updateComponents`: adjacency-list component replacement/update semantics without inferring hierarchy from visible order.
- `updateDataModel`: literal/path operations, null deletion semantics, list/map convergence, and deterministic ordering as specified.
- `deleteSurface`: idempotent teardown and cancellation of surface-scoped waits.
- Version and catalog negotiation; reject unsupported versions/catalogs explicitly.
- Incremental JSONL/stream parsing across arbitrary chunk boundaries, multiple messages per chunk, malformed-record isolation, bounded message/document size, and no partial mutation before validation.

### Client-to-server events

Support every v0.9.1 client event:

- `action` with surface/component/action identity, source component, timestamp/interaction ID supplied by Oqto, and the action's resolved typed context/data payload.
- `error` using the standard validation/runtime error shape and preserving causal presentation/surface identity.
- Client capabilities and client data-model metadata needed by the transport binding.

Do not claim Pi RPC accepts arbitrary tool-result input. Delivery semantics must be explicit:

1. **Blocking interaction:** a Pi tool remains pending; a matching authorized interaction resolves its `execute()` and Pi creates the genuine `toolResult`.
2. **Persistent/non-blocking interaction:** the initial tool returns the presentation handle; later interactions enter Pi through `pi.sendMessage()` as a typed custom message with `deliverAs: "followUp"` and `triggerTurn: true` when appropriate.
3. **Local action:** the Oqto renderer/broker handles deterministic local functions without waking Pi; only broker-authorized agent-response events cross this adapter.
4. **Headless fallback:** return/emit a stable serialized semantic event, never fake a human utterance or tool result.

### Catalog, binding, functions, validation

The adapter must transport, negotiate, and preserve the complete Basic Catalog contract rather than inventing a private component schema:

- Components: Text, Image, Icon, Video, AudioPlayer, Row, Column, List, Card, Tabs, Divider, Modal, Button, TextField, CheckBox, ChoicePicker, Slider, DateTimeInput.
- Common types: component IDs/common/accessibility attributes, ChildList adjacency/template semantics, dynamic strings/numbers/booleans/string lists, data bindings, actions, checks, and function calls.
- Two-way input binding and client/server data-model synchronization.
- Server actions versus local actions; local function expressions, nesting, validation checks, disabled-state evaluation, and standard validation errors.
- Basic functions: `formatString`, `required`, `regex`, `length`, `numeric`, `email`, `formatNumber`, `formatCurrency`, `formatDate`, `pluralize`, `openUrl`, `and`, `or`, and `not`.
- Capabilities: supported protocol versions, catalogs, functions, and client data model. Never advertise unsupported behavior.
- Preserve accessibility metadata end-to-end.

`openUrl` and any user-gesture-sensitive or side-effecting function must remain host-authorized and require genuine user activation; the Pi adapter never executes it itself.

## Security and reliability invariants

- Treat every broker frame as untrusted input: bounded framing, strict schema/version validation, no prototype-pollution keys, no unsafe deserialization, no code evaluation.
- The extension cannot grant capabilities, weaken iframe/rendering policy, register executable frontend components, select origins, or request arbitrary network access.
- Correlate interactions by stable IDs, never text, component array index, arrival order, or currently focused tab.
- At-most-once Pi delivery per Interaction ID across reconnect/replay; duplicate events are acknowledged but not delivered twice.
- A stale expected revision produces a typed conflict, not last-write-wins.
- Backpressure must be bounded; overflow fails visibly instead of dropping interactions silently.
- Structured details stored in tool/custom messages must remain branch/session-safe and serializable.
- Never log payload fields that may contain submitted secrets; diagnostics log IDs, schema/version, sizes, and result class only.

## Proof of positive outcome

Add automated tests proving:

1. Golden fixtures from the official v0.9.1 schemas validate and round-trip for every server/client envelope, common dynamic type, Basic Catalog component, and Basic Catalog function.
2. Official invalid/conformance fixtures fail closed with a stable error and produce no broker mutation.
3. Streaming parser handles every split point, coalesced records, invalid middle records, size limits, and reconnect replay.
4. A blocking presentation resolves as a real Pi tool result; cancellation/timeout/session close clean up the pending call.
5. A persistent presentation returns immediately, then delivers a later interaction exactly once as a typed custom follow-up message—not as a fake tool result or fake user message.
6. Local actions do not trigger a Pi turn.
7. Wrong Session/requester/surface, stale revision, duplicate Interaction ID, unsupported version/catalog/function, malformed binding path, and revoked capability all fail closed.
8. Secrets in form payloads are absent from logs/snapshots used by tests.
9. `bun run check` passes warning-free, and README documents setup, broker prerequisites, blocking versus persistent semantics, headless behavior, supported A2UI version, and troubleshooting.

## Boundaries

- No frontend renderer or Oqto persistence implementation in this repository.
- No MCP-first architecture; MCP may later be another adapter over the same broker operations.
- No Aethon `globalThis` host API or `new Function` frontend module loading.
- No speculative v1.0 behavior advertised under v0.9.1.

title: pi-history-search: adopt bench recall-spec v0.1
pi-history-search: adopt bench recall-spec v0.1
description:
## Goal

Make HistorySearch/HistoryGrep find needle-facts in one cheap call, per the shared spec: `~/byteowlz/bench/docs/recall-spec.md` (repo: forgejo/wismut/bench).

Real failure this encodes (2026-09-01, case `immich-admin-password` in `~/.local/share/recall-bench/`): BM25 ranked the correct session #2 on the first query, but the answer lived in a toolResult (msg 1475); results carried 60k+ chars of commands/files blobs; no msgIndex anchor was shown; a literal-vs-regex pattern mixup then produced a silent "no matches". Total: ~6 calls / ~40k tokens to fail. Grep baseline does it in 1 call / ~1.2k chars / <2s.

## Changes (in priority order)

1. **Grep pattern fallback** (grep.ts): when literal matching returns zero hits and the pattern contains regex metachars/escapes, auto-retry as regex and note the mode in output. Never bare "no matches" without listing modes tried.
2. **HistorySearch output budget**: default ≤3k chars total (spec §3): per session → id, title, ts, ONE best snippet (≤300 chars) with role + msgIndex. `commands`/`files` truncated to ≤120 chars or dropped behind a `verbose` flag. Snippet selection scans all roles (incl. tool) even when ranking is conversation-weighted.
3. **Needle mode** (spec §1): identifier-shaped queries (emails, paths, key=value, camelCase, quoted strings) route to a literal/regex scan across session files first (indexer already knows all paths); BM25 fallback on zero hits. Expose as `mode: "grep"` on HistorySearch.
4. **Always anchor**: every returned session carries the best-match msgIndex so HistoryRead(around=) is one follow-up call.

## Acceptance

- `cd ~/byteowlz/bench && just bench-internal`: case immich-admin-password PASS within ≤2 calls and ≤3k chars via the extension's query path (add a strategy adapter to bench/runner that imports the extension's functions).
- Existing tests pass; new unit tests for the fallback rule and snippet selection incl. tool roles.

title: pi-tui-rpc: drive one pi session from TUI and RPC clients simultaneously
description:
Spike: prove that a pi extension running inside a TUI-mode pi process can expose a socket-based RPC surface so an external frontend (oqto) and the TUI drive the SAME session at the same time.

Background: oqto spawns one `pi --mode rpc` per session; the TUI is a mutually exclusive mode of the same binary. Two processes on one session file diverge. The fix is one pi process owning the Session with two frontends attached. pi 2 (dev) solves this durably with multiple presentation attachments per Session; this spike is the bridge-era mechanism that must stay disposable behind oqto's PiTranslator.

Scope (spike, pi-tui-rpc extension):
- Unix-socket JSONL server started on session_start, closed on session_shutdown. Socket path: PI_TUI_RPC_SOCKET env override, else tmpdir default.
- Outbound event fanout: mirror pi extension events (agent_start/end/settled, turn_start/end, message_start/update/end, tool_execution_*, model_select, thinking_level_select, session_*, ui_prompt_start/end) to all connected clients as JSONL.
- Inbound commands: prompt/steer/follow_up (via pi.sendUserMessage with deliverAs mapping; error when streaming without behavior), abort, get_state, get_messages, lease request/release.
- Input lease: TUI is default owner. Remote takeover requires ctx.ui.confirm in the TUI. TUI typing (input event source=interactive) auto-reverts ownership. Remote commands rejected with lease_denied while TUI owns. Lease changes broadcast to clients and shown in TUI status.
- Captured ExtensionContext pattern: ctx is only available inside handlers, so stash latest ctx per session and rebind on session_start; session-control ops restricted to idle.

Positive-outcome proof (agent must run and show results):
1. bun run check (lint + typecheck) passes with the new extension.
2. bun test passes: unit tests for lease state machine (tui->remote via confirm, remote->tui on TUI input, release), protocol frame parsing (malformed lines rejected, strict LF framing), deliverAs mapping (idle prompt, streaming without behavior -> error, steer/follow_up mapping), and broadcast fanout (multiple clients, dead-client cleanup).
3. Live E2E in tmux: run `pi -e ./pi-tui-rpc/index.ts --no-session` (plus a session-file run for integrity check), connect test client:
   a. client sends prompt; client receives message stream events; TUI pane shows the same exchange (tmux capture-pane).
   b. while idle, typing in the TUI (send-keys) produces message events on the client too - proves simultaneous TUI + remote on one session.
   c. lease: client requests, TUI confirm dialog appears (tmux capture), Enter confirms, lease=remote broadcast; client prompt executes; then TUI send-keys reverts lease to tui and remote prompt gets lease_denied.
   d. streaming behavior: with a turn in flight, client prompt without streamingBehavior gets an error; with steer it is accepted and delivered.

Background: oqto spawns one `pi --mode rpc` per session; the TUI is a mutually exclusive mode of the same binary. Two processes on one session file diverge. title: pi-env-ctx: extend to v2 — read herdr env directly (multiplexer/agent + host bags), VERSION=2
description:
Extend `pi-env-ctx` to v2 of the AGENT_CTX contract (see schemas/agent-context-env, now v2). Read herdr's own env (`HERDR_*`) directly as the source of truth for the multiplexer/agent + host bags, and bump VERSION to "2".

## Why / background
- AGENT_CTX v2 was published in `byteowlz/schemas` (commit 2ed5700): producer-map layering (platform → multiplexer → harness → host), each bag optional/present-only-when-its-layer-exists.
- pi-env-ctx currently owns the harness bag only: VERSION="1", HARNESS=pi, HARNESS_SESSION_ID, MODEL, SESSION_NAME.
- Decision: do NOT split into a new extension — pi-env-ctx is byteowlz-owned and the single natural home. Quietly note `~/.pi/agent/extensions/pi-env-ctx` is a deployed copy of this repo's source.
- User accepted: `AGENT_ID = AGENT_ADDRESS = $HERDR_PANE_ID` for now; `MACHINE_ID` defaults to hostname; `AGENT_LABEL` deferred (needs async socket call to herdr for the tab/pane title).

## Scope
1. `AGENT_CTX_VERSION` → "2".
2. Multiplexer/agent bag — emit ONLY when `HERDR_ENV === "1"`:
   - `AGENT_CTX_MULTIPLEXER = "herdr"`
   - `AGENT_CTX_AGENT_ID = $HERDR_PANE_ID`
   - `AGENT_CTX_AGENT_ADDRESS = $HERDR_PANE_ID`
   - `AGENT_CTX_WORKSPACE_ID = $HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID` (opt; herdr-only setups with no oqto)
   - `AGENT_LABEL` deliberately skipped this pass.
3. Host bag — always emitted (host layer, herdr-independent):
   - `AGENT_CTX_MACHINE_ID` = herdr machine name if a suitable env exists else `os.hostname()`
   - `AGENT_CTX_NODE_HOSTNAME = os.hostname()`
   - `AGENT_CTX_OS_ARCH` = `platform/arch` mapped (x64→amd64; e.g. darwin/arm64, linux/amd64)
4. Wire into existing lifecycle: fold a `readHerdrLayer(env?, host?)`-style helper into `exportAll`/`refreshFromContext`; add all new vars to `clearOwned`.
5. Update ownership contract comment in index.ts, README.md, and tests. Use the injectable-`env` pattern in core.ts so unit tests don't touch process.env.

Out of scope: oqto/platform bag (follow-up via pi-oqto-bridge once oqto↔herdr are integrated); any herdr upstream changes.

## Positive-outcome proof
1. `bun run check` passes.
2. `bun test` passes — new unit tests cover: no herdr env → multiplexer/agent vars UNSET (undefined), harness bag still set, VERSION=2; HERDR_ENV=1 + HERDR_PANE_ID → MULTIPLEXER=herdr + AGENT_ID/ADDRESS=pane id + host bag set; os_arch mapping (x64→amd64); clearOwned removes all new vars.
3. Reinstall into `~/.pi/agent/extensions/pi-env-ctx`, `/reload`. In a herdr-managed pane, verify with `node -e` that AGENT_CTX_MULTIPLEXER=herdr, AGENT_CTX_AGENT_ADDRESS=<paneId>, AGENT_CTX_OS_ARCH set; outside herdr the multiplexer/agent vars are unset.
4. Docs: README ownership contract + a short "producer bridging: herdr" note. No version bump needed for schema (schema already v2).

(Trx issue authored from the session that designed AGENT_CTX v2; owner/tab stamped from AGENT_CTX per this exact mechanism.)

title: pi-herdr-tools: durable agent-close history + socket-subscription push close events (+ gvnr event emission)
description:
FEATURE (pi-herdr-tools): durable agent-close history + push close events, so a finished/closed subagent's record survives herdr's live-only agent list and feeds the fleet trail.

GAP (confirmed)
- herdr `agent list` is a LIVE registry: finished/closed agents drop out, so a closed subagent vanishes from the fleet view.
- pi-herdr-tools tracks subagents in ~/.pi/agent/subagent-state/<sessionId>.json (status/done/gone) but POLLS `herdr agent list` (herdr() shells out via execFileAsync); it does NOT subscribe to the socket, so it only notices a close on the next poll and only while the parent session is alive.
- No durable, queryable per-agent history; nothing feeds gvnr's event log.

FINDING (good news)
- The herdr socket API DOES emit close/exit events on its EventData subscription stream: tab_closed, pane_closed, pane_exited, pane_agent_status_changed (confirmed via `herdr api schema --output`; schemas include `event` + `subscription_event`, AgentStatus enum idle/working/blocked/done/unknown).
- So a PUSH close event is available — herdr already emits it; the extension just doesn't subscribe.

DESIGN
1. SUBSCRIBE to the herdr socket EventData stream (tab_closed / pane_closed / pane_exited / pane_agent_status_changed). Mechanism: the `herdr` CLI has no subscribe command, so either (a) open HERDR_SOCKET_PATH directly and issue the subscription JSON-RPC, or (b) add a thin socket client/helper. Correlate by pane_id/tab_id/agent to this session's tracked subagents and the current agent id.
2. On tab/pane close or agent->done, RECORD a closure: agent id + label, session, pane/tab, workspace, model, timestamps, outcome (done/closed/error).
3. RETAIN an append-only history (extend subagent-state per session, or a global subagent-history.jsonl) so it survives; expose `/subagent list` to show all (incl. done/closed) and add `/subagent history [--all]`.
4. EMIT a structured closure event to gvnr's event log (durable fleet trail: which agents ran, how they ended) with provenance stamped from AGENT_CTX (agent id/address/machine) — ties into piext-wvx0 (AGENT_CTX bridge) and gvnr event emission (never loses facts).
5. FALLBACK: keep the existing polling `done`/`gone` detection for events missed while unsubscribed (e.g. extension restarted, or agent closed before subscribe).

POSITIVE-OUTCOME PROOF
1. bun run check + tests pass.
2. Spawn a subagent, `herdr`-side close its tab: the extension records a closed outcome (via socket event) even without re-polling; `/subagent history` shows it; a closure event reaches gvnr's event log.
3. Kill the parent before the agent finishes: the closure is still recorded via the socket subscription (not just polling).
4. An agent that finishes (status done) is recorded with done + outcome.

RELATED
- piext-wvx0 (AGENT_CTX v2 bridge: agent id/address provenance).
- gvnr event-log (durable facts); pi-herdr-tools completion notification already sets `notified`.

title: pi-auto-rename: env-dependent failing test (tmp prefix) — make deterministic
description:
BUG (pi-auto-rename test): "rename still succeeds when context remains active" is flaky/fail-by-default because it depends on an ambient auto-rename.json that isn't present.

SYMPTOM
- `bun test pi-auto-rename` fails 1 of 3:
  `stale-context guard > rename still succeeds when context remains active` (index.test.ts:133)
  `expect(getSessionName().startsWith("tmp: Hello ")).toBe(true)` → received false.
- Runs fine on a machine that has the git `prefixCommand` config; empty prefix here.

ROOT CAUSE
- `loadConfig(cwd)` returns `DEFAULT_CONFIG` (prefixCommand: undefined, prefix: "") when no
  `auto-rename.json` is found in cwd, cwd/.pi, or ~/.pi/agent. `resolvePrefix` then emits an
  empty prefix, so the session name is "Hello ..." (no "tmp: ").
- The test hardcodes the expectation that the prefix is `tmp`, which is only true if the
  git `prefixCommand` ("basename $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)")
  is present in an ambient config AND run from a cwd whose git top-level basename is "tmp".
- Verified: `~/.pi/agent/auto-rename.json` absent on this host; the test is environment-dependent,
  not a production-code regression.

FIX DIRECTION (make the test deterministic)
1. Inject a `prefixCommand`/config into the test (or set the mock ctx.cwd to a real \`tmp\`-rooted
   path and write a temp `auto-rename.json`), so the prefix is deterministic regardless of the host.
2. Alternatively, mock `executeCommand` (the `execSync` boundary) to return a fixed prefix, so the
   assertion doesn't depend on the real cwd's git state or the absence of a config file.
3. Keep the assertion on the session-name shape but decoupled from ambient config.

ACCEPTANCE
- `bun test pi-auto-rename` passes on any host (config present or absent), deterministically.
- No behavior change to the extension for real users.
